The third: it refers to Jesus, so the meaning is: they did not truly kill Jesus. This is the saying of al-Hasan. Ibn al-Anbari said: "Certainty" is delayed in meaning, so the sense is: "They did not kill him, but Allah raised him to Himself with certainty."

(p-247) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: there is none of them but that he will surely believe in him. A similar usage is ﴿And there is none of you but that he will pass through it﴾ [Maryam: 71].

Regarding "the People of the Book" there are two views.

One: they are the Jews. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: they are the Jews and the Christians. This was said by al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah.

Regarding the pronoun in "in him" there are two views.

One: it refers to 'Isa (Jesus). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of scholars. The second: it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). This was said by 'Ikrimah.

Regarding the pronoun in "his death" there are two views.

One: it refers to the People of the Book. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: No Jew ever dies until he believes in 'Isa. It was said to Ibn 'Abbas: "What if he falls from the top of a house?" He said: "He will speak of it while falling." He said: In the recitation of Ubayy it is "before their death."

This is the view of Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The Jew believes before he dies, and the soul of the Christian does not depart until he testifies that 'Isa is a servant (of Allah). 'Ikrimah said: The soul of neither the Jew nor the Christian departs until he believes in Muhammad (ﷺ).

(p-248) The second: it refers to 'Isa. 'Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: When he descends to the earth, no Jew or Christian will remain, nor anyone who worships other than Allah, except that he will follow him, believe him, and testify that he is the Spirit of Allah, His Word, His servant, and His Prophet. This is the view of Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Qutaybah, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and it is related from al-Hasan as one of the two views.

(p-249) Al-Zajjaj said: This is far-fetched, given the generality of His saying: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book﴾, and those who remain at that time are a small group of them. Unless the meaning is that they all say: "The 'Isa who descends to kill the Dajjal, we believe in him."

(p-250) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾. Qatadah said: He will be a witness against them that he had conveyed the messages of his Lord, and they acknowledged servitude to Him against themselves.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 160:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews﴾. Muqatil said: Allah prohibited for the People of the Torah (al-Tawrah) usury (riba, unlawful interest) and consuming people's wealth unjustly. They did so, and they turned people away from the religion of Allah and from belief in Muhammad, peace be upon him. So Allah prohibited for them what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾ [al-An'am: 146], as a punishment for them.

Abu Sulayman said: Their wrongdoing was their breaking of their covenant, their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and what is mentioned in the verses before it.

Mujahid said, regarding ﴿and their turning many away from the way of Allah﴾: their turning themselves and others away from the truth.

Ibn Abbas said: "Their turning people away from the way of Allah" means from Islam. "Their consuming people's wealth falsely" means by lying about the religion of Allah and by taking bribes (rushā, pl. rushan, payments to pervert a ruling) for the judgment of Allah, and by altering the Books which Allah sent down, so that they might perpetuate their livelihood (al-ma'kal).

Allah's words: ﴿And We have prepared﴾, meaning: We have readied for the disbelievers, that is, the Jews. It was said: He said "from among them" (minhum) because He knew that some of them would believe and so be safe from the punishment.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 162:

His saying, Most High: ﴿But those firmly grounded in knowledge﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: This is an exception for the believers among the People of the Book. As for "those firmly grounded" (al-rasikhun), they are those steadfast in knowledge. Abu Sulayman said: They are ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and those who believed with him, and those among the People of the Gospel who believed and who came with Jaʿfar from Abyssinia, and the believers, meaning the Companions of the Messenger of God. As for His saying: ﴿and those who establish the prayer﴾, they are those who perform it as they were commanded.

Regarding the case (naṣb) of "al-muqimin" (those who establish) there are four opinions.

The first: that it is a mistake by the scribe. This is the view of ʿAʾisha, and it is narrated from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan that he said: "There is a lahn (grammatical error) in the Mushaf which the Arabs will correct with their tongues." Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrima and al-Jahdari read: "wal-muqimuna al-salah" with the waw.

Al-Zajjaj said: The saying of the one who says it is a mistake is very far-fetched, because those who collected the Qur'an were the people of the language and the model, so how would they leave in the Book of God something that others would have to correct? This should not be attributed to them. Ibn al-Anbari said: The hadith of ʿUthman is not authentic, because it is not connected (munqatiʿ), and it is impossible that ʿUthman would delay something corrupt so that someone after him would correct it.

The second: that it is in coordination (nasaq) with "ma" (what), and the meaning is: they believe in what has been sent down to you and in those who establish the prayer. It was said: they are the angels; and it was said: the prophets.

The third: that it is in coordination with the hā' and mīm in His saying "minhum" (from among them). The meaning then is: "But those firmly grounded in knowledge among them, and those who establish the prayer, believe in what has been sent down to you." Al-Zajjaj said: This is weak according to the grammarians; a apparent genitive noun is not coordinated with a pronoun in the genitive except in poetry.

The fourth: that it is in the accusative by way of praise (madḥ). The meaning is: "Mention those who establish the prayer, and they are those who give the zakat." They recited:

Let not my people be far away, those who are the poison of enemies and the calamity of the slaughtered camels,

Those who alight at every battlefield, and those who are good at tying the waistcloths.

This is according to the meaning: "Mention those who alight, and they are the good ones." From this is your saying: "I passed by Zayd the generous" — if you intend to distinguish him from others, the genitive is the usual form; if you intend praise and commendation, then if you wish you may put it in the accusative, saying "bi-Zayd al-karim," as if you said: "Mention the generous one"; and if you wish you may put it in the nominative, meaning: "He is the generous one." And you say: "Your people came to me, those who feed in times of scarcity, and those who relieve in hardships," according to the meaning: "Mention those who feed, and they are those who relieve." This opinion is the choice of al-Khalil and Sibawayh.

These are the opinions which al-Zajjaj related, and he chose this last opinion.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 163:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: ʿAdiyy ibn Zayd and Sukayn said: "O Muhammad, we do not know that Allah has sent down anything to a human after Musa," so this verse was revealed. We have already discussed the meaning of revelation (waḥy) in (Al ʿImran), and it was mentioned there.

Ishaq is a non-Arabic name, even though it matches an Arabic word; it is said: Asḥaqahu Allah, yasḥaquhu, isḥaqan. Yaʿqub is non-Arabic. As for al-yaʿqub, which is the male partridge, and it is the qabaj, it is Arabic; thus I read it to our shaykh Abu Mansur al-Lughawi (p-255). Ayyub is non-Arabic, and Yunus is a non-Arabic name. Abu ʿUbayda said: it is said Yunus and Yunis, with the nun vowelled with a damma and a kasra. Abu Zayd al-Ansari related from the Arabs a hamza with the kasra, the damma and the fatha. Al-Farra' said: Yunus with a damma on the nun without hamza is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and some of Bani Asad say Yu'nus with hamza, and some of Bani ʿUqayl say Yunas with a fatha on the nun without hamza. The well-known reading is Yunus with a damma on the nun without hamza. Ibn Mas'ud, Qatada, Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and Talha read Yu'nis with a kasra on the nun and with hamza. Abu al-Jawza', Abu ʿImran and al-Jahdari read Yunas with a fatha on the nun without hamza. Abu al-Mutawakkil read Yu'nas with a fatha on the nun and with hamza. Abu al-Simak al-ʿAdawi read Yunis with a kasra on the nun without hamza. ʿAmr ibn Dinar read Yu'nus with a damma on the nun and with hamza. Harun is a non-Arabic name, and the mention of the rest of the prophets has already passed.

As for al-Zabur, most reciters read it with a fatha on the zay. Abu Razin, Abu Raja', al-Aʿmash and Hamza read it with a damma on the zay. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads it with a fatha on the zay means a book (kitab), and whoever reads it with a damma means books (kutub). The mention of "Dawud" means: do not deny the preference of Muhammad through the Qur'an, for Allah gave Dawud the Zabur. Abu ʿAli said: it seems Hamza took the book of Dawud as sections (anhaʾ), made each section a zubur, and then pluralized it, saying zuburan. Ibn Qutayba said: al-Zabur is fa'ul in the sense of maf'ul, as you say halub and rakub in the sense of mahlub and markub, and it derives from your saying: zabartu al-kitab azburuhu zabran, when you write it. He said: there is another dialect, al-Zubur with a damma on the zay, as if it were a plural.

(p-256) His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses directly﴾. The emphasis of "spoke" (kallama) with the verbal noun (takliman) indicates that he truly heard the speech of Allah. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi narrated, saying: I heard Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar say: I heard Thaʻlab say: "Had Allah, exalted is He, not emphasized the verb with the verbal noun, it would have been permissible for it to mean what one of us says to another: 'I have spoken to so-and-so for you,' meaning, 'I wrote a letter to him' or 'I sent a messenger to him.' But when He said takliman, it could only be speech heard from Allah."

God's words: ﴿So that people will have no argument against God﴾, that is: so that they cannot argue, in abandoning monotheism (tawhid) and obedience, that there were no messengers, because these matters are only made obligatory through the messengers.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 166:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But Allah bears witness﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are two reports.

(p-257) One of them: "The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon a group of the Jews and said: 'I swear by Allah, you certainly know that I am the Messenger of Allah.' They said: 'We do not know that.' So this verse was revealed." This is the statement of Ibn Abbas.

The second: "The leaders of the people of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'We asked the Jews about you, and they claimed that they do not recognize you. So bring us someone who will bear witness that Allah has sent you.' So this verse was revealed." This is the statement of Ibn al-Sa'ib.

Al-Zajjaj said: al-Shahid (the witness) is one who makes clear what he testifies to. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made that clear, and He knows, along with His making it clear, that it is the truth. Regarding the meaning of ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾ there are three opinions.

The first: He sent it down while His knowledge is in it. This is the saying of al-Zajjaj.

The second: He sent it down from His knowledge. This was mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

The third: He sent it down to you with knowledge from Him that you are His chosen one from among His creation. This is the saying of Ibn Jarir.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the angels bear witness﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions.

One of them: they bear witness that Allah sent it down. The second: they bear witness to your truthfulness.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah suffices as a witness﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the "ba" (bi) has entered as an emphasizer, and the meaning is: be content with Allah in His testimony.

(p-258) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾. Muqatil and others said: they are the Jews, who disbelieved in Muhammad and averted people from Islam. Abu Sulayman said: Their averting [people] from Islam was their saying to the polytheists and to their followers: "We do not find the description of Muhammad in our Book."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 168–169:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged﴾. Muqatil and others said: They are also the Jews, who disbelieved in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Regarding the wrongdoing mentioned here, there are two opinions.

The first: that it is polytheism (shirk); this was said by Muqatil. The second: that it is their denial of the description of Muhammad, the Prophet (ﷺ), in their Book.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾, meaning those among them who die upon disbelief. Abu Sulayman said: Allah would never conceal from them their evil deeds, but rather He would disgrace them in this world and punish them with killing, exile and captivity, and in the Hereafter with the Fire. ﴿Nor would He guide them to a path﴾ by which they could be saved.

Muqatil said: a path to guidance. ﴿And that is ever for Allah, easy﴾, meaning: their punishment is easy for Allah.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 168–169:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged﴾. Muqatil and others said: They are also the Jews, who disbelieved in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Regarding the wrongdoing mentioned here, there are two opinions.

The first: that it is polytheism (shirk); this was said by Muqatil. The second: that it is their denial of the description of Muhammad, the Prophet (ﷺ), in their Book.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah would never forgive them﴾, meaning those among them who die upon disbelief. Abu Sulayman said: Allah would never conceal from them their evil deeds, but rather He would disgrace them in this world and punish them with killing, exile and captivity, and in the Hereafter with the Fire. ﴿Nor would He guide them to a path﴾ by which they could be saved.

Muqatil said: a path to guidance. ﴿And that is ever for Allah, easy﴾, meaning: their punishment is easy for Allah.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 170:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So believe; it is better for you﴾. Al-Zajjaj said, on the authority of al-Khalil (ibn Ahmad) and all the Basran grammarians: it is in the accusative (nasb) by virtue of being taken as a response to its meaning (al-haml ʿala maʿnahu), because when you say, "Desist, it is better for you" (intahi khayran laka), while you are turning him away from a matter and directing him into another, the meaning is: "Desist, and come to what is better for you, and enter into what is better for you." Al-Khalil and Sibawayh recited the verse of ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿa:

؎ So make an appointment with him at the two acacia trees of Malik, or al-Ruba, whichever of the two is easier.

It is as if he said: "Come to a place that is easier."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾. That is: He is Free of need of you and of your faith. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of what will occur of faith or disbelief, ﴿Wise﴾ in your obligation (taklif), together with His knowledge of what will occur from you.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 171:

(p-260) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion﴾. Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the Christians of Najran, al-Sayyid and al-'Aqib, and those with them. The majority hold that the intended meaning of this verse is the Christians. al-Hasan said: It was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians. Ghuluww (excess, extremism): exceeding the proper limit and going beyond bounds; from it comes the expression "ghala al-si'r" (the price soared). al-Zajjaj said: Ghuluww is going beyond the measure in wrongdoing. The Christians' excess concerning 'Isa (Jesus) is the saying of some of them that he is God, the saying of some that he is the Son of God, and the saying of some that he is the third of three. According to al-Hasan's view, the Jews' excess concerning him is their saying that he was born out of wedlock. Some scholars said: Do not commit excess in your religion by increasing in strictness regarding it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not say about God except the truth﴾, i.e., do not say that God has a partner (p-261) or a son or a wife. We have already mentioned the meaning of "al-Masih" (the Messiah) and "al-Kalima" (the Word) in (Al 'Imran).

Regarding the meaning of ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾ there are seven opinions.

The first: that he is a spirit from among the spirits of bodies. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: When God took the covenant from the children of Adam, 'Isa was a spirit from those spirits, so He sent him to Maryam, and she conceived him.

The second: that "the spirit" means the breath, and it was called a spirit because it came into being from the breath of Jibril into the shift of Maryam. From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rumma:

"I said to him: Raise it to yourself and revive it with your spirit, and make for her a measured portion of it."

This is the saying of Abu Rawq.

The third: that the meaning of ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾ is a living person, made alive by God.

The fourth: that "the spirit" is mercy, so the meaning is "and a mercy from Him." Similar to it is ﴿and He strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22].

The fifth: that "the spirit" here is Jibril. The meaning is: God cast it to Maryam, and the one who cast it is a spirit from Him. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi mentioned these three opinions.

(p-262) The sixth: that He called him a spirit because people are given life through him just as they are given life by spirits, and for this reason the Qur'an was called a spirit. This was mentioned by al-Qadi Abu Ya'la.

The seventh: that "the spirit" is revelation. God revealed to Maryam, giving her good news of it, revealed to Jibril to breathe into her shift, and revealed to the essence of 'Isa that: "Be," and he was. A similar usage is ﴿He sends down the angels with the spirit of His command﴾ [al-Nahl: 2], i.e., with the revelation. This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi.

As for His saying "from Him," it is an idafa of honour, as you say "the House of God," and the meaning is "from His command." Something close to it is His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [al-Jathiya: 13].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not say, "Three"﴾. al-Zajjaj said: It is put in the nominative by implying: do not say "our gods are three." ﴿Indeed, God is but one God﴾, i.e., He is only one God. ﴿Exalted is He above having a son﴾: the meaning of "Subhanahu" is His being declared free from having a son. Abu Sulayman said: ﴿And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs﴾, i.e., a guardian over His creation, managing their affairs for them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah﴾. The occasion of its revelation (sabab al-nuzul): "The delegation of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, 'O Muhammad, you have not mentioned our companion.' He said, 'And who is your companion?' They said, 'Jesus.' He said, 'And what should I say about him?' They said, 'He is the servant of Allah.' They said, 'Rather, he is Allah.' He said, 'Indeed, there is no shame for him in being a servant of Allah.' They said, 'Yes indeed.' Then this verse was revealed." Narrated by Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of yastankif is (p. 263) ya'naf (to be too proud, to disdain). Its root in the language is from nakaftu al-dam'a (I wiped away the tear), when you move the tear away with your finger from your cheek. The poet said:

"They departed, and had it not been for what they reminded of among them, from the alliance, the tear would not have been wiped away from your two eyes."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nor the angels brought near﴾. Ibn Abbas said: They are the bearers of the Throne.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 173:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So He will give them their rewards﴾, i.e., the reward of their deeds, ﴿and will increase them from His bounty﴾, meaning the multiplication of good deeds.

Ibn Mas'ud narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿So He will give them their rewards﴾, that he said: "They will enter Paradise. And He will increase them from His bounty: intercession (shafa'ah) for those who deserved the Fire from among those who did good to them (al-ma'ruf) in the world."

(p-264) His words, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord﴾. Regarding "al-burhan" (the proof) there are three opinions.

The first: that it is the argument (al-hujjah). This was said by Mujahid and al-Suddi. The second: that it is the Qur'an. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: that it is the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). This was said by Sufyan al-Thawri. As for "a manifest light" (al-nur al-mubin), it is the Qur'an, as said by Qatadah. He called it "light" because rulings become clear through it, just as things become clear by light.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 4, verse 175:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And hold fast to Him﴾, meaning: they clung to Him. There are two opinions regarding the pronoun in "bihi" (to Him).

The first: it refers to the light, which is the Qur'an. This was said by Ibn Jurayj. The second: it refers to God, may He be exalted. This was said by Muqatil. There are two opinions regarding "mercy."

The first: it is Paradise. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil. The second: it is mercy itself, and the meaning is: "He will show them mercy." This was said by Abu Sulayman. There are two opinions regarding "bounty" (fadl).

The first: it is provision in Paradise. This was said by Muqatil. The second: it is kindness (ihsan). This was said by Abu Sulayman.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾, meaning: He grants them success in reaching the straight way. Ibn al-Hanafiyya said: "The straight path is the religion of God."

(p-٢٦٥) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾ (yastaftunaka). There are two accounts of the occasion of its revelation.

The first is that it was revealed concerning Jabir ibn Abd Allah. Abu al-Zubayr narrated from Jabir, who said: "I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to visit me, he and Abu Bakr [while they were both walking]. He found me unconscious, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed ablution and then poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained consciousness. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how should I deal with my property, given that I have nine sisters and I have no child?' He did not answer me with anything. Then he went out and left me, then he came back to me and said, 'O Jabir, I do not see you dying from this illness of yours. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed concerning your sisters, and has assigned them two-thirds.' Then he recited to me this verse: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala (one who leaves neither descendant nor ascendant)﴾." Jabir used to say, "This verse was revealed concerning me."

The second is that the Companions were concerned to clarify the matter of the kalala, so they asked the Prophet of Allah about it, and this verse was revealed. This is the saying of Qatada. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'How do we give inheritance to the kalala?' He said: 'Has Allah not already made that clear?' Then he recited: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance as kalala [and has no ascendant or descendant]﴾. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala.﴾"

(p-٢٦٦) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If a man dies﴾, meaning: dies. ﴿And he has no child﴾, meaning: nor any parent. He mentioned only one of the two, and what indicates the omitted part is that the ruling is about the kalala, who is one who has neither child nor parent.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he has a sister﴾, meaning from his father and mother ﴿then for her is half of what he leaves﴾ when she is alone ﴿and he inherits from her﴾, meaning he takes the whole inheritance of the sister if she has no child and no parent. This is the brother from the father and mother, or from the father alone. ﴿And if there are two sisters﴾, meaning two sisters. Al-Akhfash was asked: "What is the benefit of His saying 'two' (ithnatayn) and 'they were' (kanatā), since it can only be explained as two?" He said: "It conveys a number free of any description, because 'kanatā' could be 'young' (saghīratayn), or 'free' (hurratayn), or 'righteous' (ṣāliḥatayn), or 'wicked' (ṭāliḥatayn). So when He said 'two' (ithnatayn), this is the unrestricted number, whatever description they have." ﴿Then for them are two-thirds﴾ of the estate of their deceased brother. ﴿And if there are [brothers and sisters]﴾, meaning: the heirs who are left behind.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾. Ibn Qutayba said: "It means: so that you do not go astray." Al-Zajjaj said: "In this there are two opinions. The first: 'an lā tuḍillū' (that you not go astray), with lā (not) being implied. The second: 'karāhiyata an tuḍillū' (out of dislike that you go astray), and this is the view of the Basran grammarians." Ibn Jurayj said: "That you go astray regarding the matters of inheritance."
